title: Buddhism, Kant, Science
content_html:
Buddhism, Kant, Science

Buddhism - direct experiential access
Kant - limits of knowledge
Science - empirical/model-based

Kant vs. Buddhism: filtered vs. direct
Buddhism vs. Science: direct insight vs. models
Kant vs. Science: unknowable noumenon vs. pragmatic models

Buddhism

  • Mind can access reality directly through meditative insight.
  • Sees impermanence, suffering, non-self, and dependent origination as direct truths.
  • Epistemic optimism: filters can be transcended.
  • Knowledge = liberation (pragmatic soteriology).

Kant

  • Mind structures experience via categories (space, time, causality).
  • We only know phenomena, not noumena.
  • Epistemic humility: strict limits on knowledge.
  • Goal = map boundaries of reason, not transcend them.

Science

  • Knowledge advances by building models tested against experience.
  • Emphasis on prediction and correction rather than direct access.
  • Pragmatic: models need not mirror reality but must work.
  • Structural realism: science captures structure, not essence.

References
